verdict.root_cause: A platform-automation traffic-shaping sidecar was attached to cartservice's network namespace at ~09:35:58, imposing a fixed 300ms/0ms-jitter egress delay on eth0 and never removed in the window [tr_73e8163729ef]. Traces show exactly that signature: a tight ~300-310ms additive penalty on every cart egress call and ~303ms of caller-side self-time in frontend's and checkoutservice's CartService client spans, stacking to ~906-1225ms across multi-hop checkouts, while cartservice's own handler self-time stays at 0.5-1.1ms against a sub-millisecond 09:11-09:13 baseline [tr_08e03d8a1691]. cartservice is otherwise healthy and serving [tr_3e37a2185753], so what callers suffer is waiting on the cart hop; checkoutservice, which crosses that hop repeatedly, tips from slow to failing with an error ratio two orders of magnitude over a clean baseline while every other downstream stays at 0-18ms [tr_b4a881275afa, tr_08e03d8a1691]. Removing the shaping sidecar is what stops it.
verdict.reasoning: The change record places an unreverted 300ms fixed-delay shaping container on cartservice's network namespace ~3 minutes before onset, with an identical earlier episode showing it is a repeating automated pattern [tr_73e8163729ef]. Traces match that injection quantitatively: a near-constant band with no spread, additive per hop, visible on both sides of the cart hop, with cart handler self-time unchanged - which excludes GC/contention, cart CPU saturation, retries and any gradual ramp [tr_08e03d8a1691]. Blame direction follows the wait: frontend and checkout alerted after cart and are the services that block on it [tr_b4a881275afa]. Class is dependency_latency, not bad_config, because the rule does not name a wrong address or limit - it inserts wall-clock delay, and the wait is the failure. Not bad_deploy: the v1.2.1 hotfix was reverted ~14 min before onset with no later image update. Not a cache misconfig: the sole REDIS_ADDR edit reverted ~4.5h earlier [tr_73e8163729ef]. Cart's own error-ratio series is unusable, empty in both windows from a pre-existing instrumentation gap [tr_f6b9bc0254e0].
open_questions: checkoutservice's error-ratio change point is 09:17:15, ~19 minutes before the sidecar was attached [tr_b4a881275afa, tr_73e8163729ef]; injected cart latency cannot explain degradation that predates it, so a second concurrent fault or an effect of the 09:15/09:25 image cycle is unexcluded.

No checkoutservice latency series or timeout config was retrieved, so 'cart wait exceeds checkout deadline therefore checkout errors' is inferred from trace durations rather than measured; the failing calls' status codes were never read.

No dispatches on frontend or loadgenerator despite both alerting, and 4 unmeasured edges were crossed; whether the sidecar is still attached, or will be re-attached by automation after removal, is also unknown.

alternatives.root_cause: checkoutservice carries an independent fault beginning 09:17:15 and the cart delay only worsened an already-failing service.
alternatives.why_not: The earlier change point is real [tr_b4a881275afa], but no checkout-side mechanism was identified, and slow traces attribute ~1208ms and ~1225ms to checkout->cart hops while all other downstreams stay at 0-18ms [tr_08e03d8a1691]. Plausibly a second concurrent fault, not a replacement.

alternatives.root_cause: The thrice-rolled v1.2.1 cartservice hotfix left cartservice in a degraded state that the shaping sidecar merely coincided with.
alternatives.why_not: The hotfix was already reverted ~14 minutes before onset with no subsequent image update [tr_73e8163729ef], and the inflation sits in egress and inbound hop latency rather than cart application code [tr_08e03d8a1691], which no image version would produce as a fixed zero-jitter offset.

proposal.expected_effect: Detaching the traffic-shaping sidecar removes the fixed 300ms/0ms-jitter eth0 delay. In Tempo, cartservice Redis client spans should fall from the ~300-310ms band to the 0.2-0.7ms of the 09:11-09:13 baseline, and frontend/checkoutservice CartService client self-time from ~303ms (~906ms stacked) to low single-digit ms. Secondarily, checkoutservice error ratio should fall from ~0.18 toward its ~0.0009 baseline.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if fresh cart traces still carry the ~300ms penalty 3-5 min after recreate: the shaping was not in the reverted config, or platform-automation re-attached it as in the 04:44-04:53 episode. Partially falsified if cart latency normalizes but checkoutservice error ratio stays elevated, confirming the unexplained 09:17:15 change point as a second fault this does not touch.
proposal.risk: The revert may restore a snapshot older than 09:35:57.97 and reintroduce the alternate REDIS_ADDR or the reverted v1.2.1 image, converting a latency fault into a connectivity or code fault on a currently healthy service. Operator must confirm the snapshot is the state immediately before the sidecar attach. The recreate also drops in-flight carts.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice, plus its callers frontend and checkoutservice, which see connection resets and a brief error burst during the recreate; both already alerting, so that burst must not be read as the fix failing. loadgenerator sees the same via frontend.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Multiple services alerted within seconds spanning cart, checkout and frontend, which is more than a single isolated warning and cannot be dismissed. The cart-first ordering with downstream checkout/frontend following suggests a shared dependency or backing store, but evidence is needed.
